title: 1 dead, homes swept away as Hurricane Lala brings heavy rain to Hawaii’s Big Island
facts: One person died in a storm-related car crash during Hurricane Lala on Hawaii's Big Island.
Two homes in Naalehu were swept away by floodwaters from Hurricane Lala.
Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda initiated search and rescue operations in the Alihu and Waiheno areas.
PowerOutage.us reported that more than 125,000 utility customers in Hawaii lost electrical power.
Maximum sustained winds reached 75 mph during Hurricane Lala, classifying it as a Category 1 hurricane.
The National Weather Service issued a flash flood warning for the Kau District on Hawaii's Big Island.
Hawaii Governor Josh Green initiated procedures to request a major disaster declaration.
Honolulu Ocean Safety Department Director Kurt Lager reported that lifeguards completed 59 water rescues.
Michael Brennan serves as the director of the National Hurricane Center.
National Hurricane Center meteorologist Joseph Clark stated that Hurricane Lala's eye passed south of Hawaii without direct landfall.
National Weather Service meteorologist Vanessa Almanza reported that rainfall on the Big Island reached up to 25 inches at high elevations.
The Big Island was placed under a hurricane warning during the storm.
Tropical storm warnings were issued for Maui, Molokai, Lanai, Kahoolawe, Oahu, Kauai, and Niihau.
A Category 3 hurricane previously struck the Big Island of Hawaii in 1871.
Hurricane Iniki made landfall on Kauai as a Category 4 hurricane in 1992, causing $3 billion in damage.
